body:
Verified: {log_dir}/{session}.log persists after the session is gone, with epoch timestamps and the events that matter — daemon started, client connected (total=N), leader set, resize rows/cols, run command, client disconnected (remaining=N), kill received, SIGHUP, deleting socket, daemon loop shutdown.

Caveat that shapes any monitor: every CLI call briefly connects as a client, so a poller writes connect/disconnect pairs into the log it is reading. Polling ls is not free, it is visible and it is noisy — an argument for reading on demand and for keeping the reader stateless (d-shape).

Also: these are debug logs, enabled by default and not disableable in this release, so the trail is an accident of the release rather than a supported interface. Do not build on it; do read it when something went wrong.
title: per-session logs are a durable event trail, with one caveat
